feed.title: US jury says Apple owes record $5.7 billion in haptic technology patent case
feed.summary: A US jury has ruled that Apple must pay over $5.7 billion to San Diego-based Taction for infringing on its haptic technology patents used in iPhones and Apple Watches. Apple disputes the verdict, stating its Taptic Engine is fundamentally different from Taction's technology, and plans to appeal what is reportedly the largest patent infringement verdict to date in the country.

feed.title: Musk's X Corp and SpaceXAI Drop Apple From AI Antitrust Fight. Is One Legal Headache Gone for the iPhone Maker?
feed.summary: Elon Musk's companies, X Corp and SpaceXAI, have dismissed their antitrust claims against Apple, removing the iPhone maker from a lawsuit that challenged its integration of OpenAI's ChatGPT. This development removes a significant legal challenge for Apple as it further develops its AI strategy with new Siri AI features and collaborations beyond OpenAI.

feed.title: Apple Hit With $5.7 Billion Patent Verdict Over iPhone, Apple Watch Haptics

feed.title: TikTok reaches first state settlement over teen safety claims
feed.summary: TikTok has reached its first state settlement with Alabama over claims that the platform endangered children and misled consumers about its safety. The agreement mandates new usage limits and enhanced age verification for Alabama users, including a two-hour daily time limit and pauses after 15 minutes of use. TikTok will pay Alabama at least $100 million, potentially rising to $300 million if other states join similar agreements.

feed.title: Russian Strikes on Ukrainian Data Centers Leave 100,000 Households Without Internet
feed.summary: Russian forces have broadened their attacks in Ukraine to include data centers and internet providers, resulting in four deaths and leaving approximately 100,000 households without internet access. This campaign targets critical digital infrastructure, raising questions about the legality of striking dual-use facilities that house both military and civilian services. Ukrainian officials emphasize the network's resilience due to its decentralized architecture, though local disruptions and increased costs are anticipated.

feed.summary: Apple Inc. faced a labor dispute in Italy as its Apple Store employees went on strike on the global launch day of the iPhone 18 Pro. feed.title: Apple (AAPL) Eyes an Apple Pay Launch in India. How Much can it Grow Without UPI?
feed.summary: Apple is preparing to launch Apple Pay in India next month, starting with Axis Bank credit cards, after the Reserve Bank of India changed regulations to allow biometric authentication for card payments. While this removes a significant obstacle, Apple Pay will initially only support Visa and Mastercard credit cards and not India's dominant Unified Payments Interface (UPI) system, which accounts for 84% of digital payments. This strategy allows Apple to enter the market gradually, but its growth potential without UPI integration and broader bank partnerships may be limited, making it primarily an ecosystem-retention initiative rather than a major near-term revenue catalyst.

feed.title: Apple's $1.25M gift card scam settlement could pay Canadians who lost money to phone fraudsters since 2016
feed.summary: Apple has agreed to a $1.25 million class-action settlement for Canadians who lost money to gift card scams since 2016. The lawsuit alleges Apple could have done more to prevent fraudsters from redeeming iTunes, App Store, or Apple Music gift cards obtained through imposter scams. While Apple denies wrongdoing, eligible Canadians who never received a full refund may receive partial compensation once the settlement is approved and a distribution protocol is established.
